supportingMedia.value: An established BGP peer must be able to send IPv6 FlowSpec to a receiving flow6 channel configured with "validate yes". A suitable unicast route from that peer must be present in the base table. Propagation additionally requires an export policy permitting the rule. Data-plane impact depends on downstream support for, acceptance of, and enforcement of the FlowSpec match and action.

configurations.value: An established BGP peer must be able to send IPv6 FlowSpec to a receiving flow6 channel configured with "validate yes". A suitable unicast route from that peer must be present in the base table. Propagation additionally requires an export policy permitting the rule. Data-plane impact depends on downstream support for, acceptance of, and enforcement of the FlowSpec match and action.

descriptions.value: An IPv6 FlowSpec validation bypass in the CZ.NIC BIRD Internet Routing Daemon allows an established BGP peer to inject FlowSpec rules matching destinations outside the address space authorized by the unicast-route validation procedure. With validation enabled on the receiving flow6 channel, BIRD fails to reject a destination prefix component with a nonzero offset, contrary to RFC 8956 section 5. It validates a reconstructed prefix with zero-filled skipped bits, although the original FlowSpec component can match a broader set of IPv6 addresses. Given a suitable unicast route from the peer, the rule can pass validation and, where export policy permits, be propagated to downstream peers. Downstream enforcement may cause unauthorized traffic filtering or redirection.

descriptions.description: CWE-1284 Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input

supportingMedia.value: Apply upstream commit 7cf75587b6f38b87849fe192bf5dfd124b7702bc or a verified branch-specific backport. The fix requires the original IPv6 destination-prefix component to have offset zero before it can pass FlowSpec validation. The first fixed release has not yet been verified.

descriptions.value: The Bootstrap Shortcodes plugin for WordPress before 3.4.6 is vulnerable to stored XSS via the id attribute of the [bs_tcontent] shortcode. The bs_tcontent() shortcode handler in inc/bs_tabs.php emits the id attribute value into an unquoted HTML attribute. esc_attr() is applied, but it does not encode space characters, so a space in the supplied value terminates the attribute and any following text is parsed as additional HTML attributes, including JavaScript event handlers. This allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to inject arbitrary web script that executes in the browser of any user who views the page and interacts with the injected element.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

supportingMedia.value: Update the Bootstrap Shortcodes plugin to version 3.4.6 or later.

solutions.value: Update the Bootstrap Shortcodes plugin to version 3.4.6 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Until updated, deactivate the plugin or do not allow untrusted Contributor/Author-level users to publish content containing the [bs_tcontent] shortcode.

The HTTP/3 parser does not check that the received body length matches a previously announced content-length when the stream is closed via a frame with an empty payload. This can cause desynchronization issues with the backend server and could be used for request smuggling. The earliest affected version is 2.6.

cna.title: Gitea API disclosure of private user social graph, keys and stars

descriptions.value: Seven Gitea API routes under `/api/v1/users/{username}` (followers, following, following/{target}, starred, subscriptions, keys and gpg_keys) were registered without the `individualPermsChecker` middleware that enforces the visibility of the target user. An authenticated user could therefore read the followers, following list, starred and watched repositories and public SSH and GPG keys of a user with limited or private visibility, whom they could not otherwise see. The issue was fixed in 1.27.3 and 28.0.0 and disclosed with 28.2.0.

cna.title: Gitea label deletion across repository and organization IDs

descriptions.value: Deleting a label compared the ID of the repository in the request against the organization ID of organization labels, and the two ID sequences overlap. A user with write access to the issues of a repository could therefore delete the labels of an organization that has the same numeric ID as that repository. Labels are now deleted only within their own repository or organization.
